intent: Create a Pet Shop Management System to manage customers and their pets. Each customer may have multiple pets, with information such as name, species, breed, sex, age, size, and relevant notes. The system should provide a preloaded catalog of the most common dog and cat breeds, while also allowing users to add new breeds. The breed is a separate entity with a type (the species: dog, cat, etc.); a pet has a single breed field, filtered by its species. Vaccines: the shop registers the vaccines it uses (name, laboratory, diseases covered) and each batch it buys (lot number unique per vaccine, manufacture and expiry dates, doses bought); a batch past its expiry date is expired and can no longer be chosen. Each vaccination of a pet records the vaccine, an available batch, the date applied, the next dose date and who applied it; staff and the pet's owner are alerted a configurable number of days (default 2) before the next dose. Grooming and care: the shop keeps a catalog of services with a price, and books appointments for a pet with one or more services; an appointment moves from scheduled to in service, ready for pickup and done, can be cancelled by whoever holds the cancel permission, and becomes a no-show the day after if nobody came. The owner is reminded the day before and told when the pet is ready. A service may require the pet's vaccines to be up to date, and then check-in is refused while a vaccination is overdue. Customers buy packages of credits for a service, used by appointment lines. Each visit can record the pet's weight. A dashboard and reports summarise revenue, services, pets and vaccines due; a vaccination card and an appointment receipt are generated as PDFs. Customers use a portal to see their pets, vaccinations and appointments, request an appointment and confirm one. The pet shop has no dashboard and no agenda of its own: its reports are cards on the office Dashboard extension, and every appointment and every next vaccine dose is mirrored as an item of the Calendar extension, where dragging an appointment reschedules it.

entities.name: Customer
entities.description: A pet owner who brings pets to the shop.

tabs.because: The shop keeps a dated running log about each customer (calls, complaints, agreements), separate from the one free-text Notes field.
Customers hand over files the shop must keep with their record: signed consent forms, ID copies, invoices.
The shop labels customers in its own vocabulary (VIP, late payer, prefers WhatsApp) to filter and find them.

entities.name: Pet
entities.description: An animal owned by a customer. Its breed is one reference to Breed, and the form offers only the breeds of the pet's species.

fields.label: Age (years)
fields.expression: if(isEmpty(birthDate), null, floor(((year(today()) - year(birthDate)) * 12 + month(today()) - month(birthDate) - if(day(today()) < day(birthDate), 1, 0)) / 12))

fields.label: Age (months)
fields.expression: if(isEmpty(birthDate), null, ((year(today()) - year(birthDate)) * 12 + month(today()) - month(birthDate) - if(day(today()) < day(birthDate), 1, 0)) % 12)

fields.label: Photo
fields.description: A picture of the animal, shown as the avatar on its card so staff recognise it at a glance.

tabs.because: Each visit adds an observation about the animal (behaviour, grooming, health), and a dated log keeps them apart instead of overwriting one text.
A pet carries files of its own: vet reports, photos, the paper vaccination card.
The shop labels pets in its own vocabulary (aggressive, allergic, senior) so staff spot them at a glance and filter by them.

entities.name: Breed
entities.description: A breed of one species. The shop starts with the most common dog and cat breeds and adds its own.

entities.name: Vaccine
entities.description: A vaccine product the shop applies, e.g. a rabies or a polyvalent vaccine, from one laboratory.

keys.name: name-laboratory
keys.message: This laboratory already has a vaccine with this name.

entities.name: VaccineBatch
entities.description: One purchased batch (lot) of a vaccine. Its lot number is unique within the vaccine, and once its expiry date has passed it is expired and no longer offered for a vaccination.

keys.name: lot
keys.message: This vaccine already has a batch with this lot number.

entities.name: Vaccination
entities.description: One dose of a vaccine applied to a pet, from an available batch, with the date of the next dose and when to remind about it. The reminder itself is a workflow on the kernel clock (pet-vaccine-reminder in vaccines.ts): a vaccination has no states, so the model's behavior block cannot describe it. The batch is chosen through an options filter (only available batches of the chosen vaccine), a form rule the model cannot express either. Its status is current until the day after the next dose, when it becomes overdue; a later dose of the same vaccine for the same pet marks it renewed and records which dose renewed it. Its next dose is mirrored as an item of the Calendar extension.

entities.name: Service
entities.description: Something the shop does to a pet and charges for: a bath, a grooming, a nail trim.

keys.name: name
keys.message: There is already a service with this name.

entities.name: Appointment
entities.description: A visit booked for one pet on a day and time, with one line per service. Numbered per year. A tab of the pet and its own menu entry. Each appointment is mirrored as an item of the Calendar extension (calendar.ts), kept in step on every save and delete; dragging the item to another day reschedules the appointment.

tabs.because: The receipt generated when the pet is picked up is attached here, and shared with the owner in the portal.

entities.name: AppointmentItem
entities.description: One service of an appointment, at the price charged that day — or paid with a credit of one of the pet's packages.

fields.label: Price
fields.reason: The price charged on the day of the appointment; a later change to the service price must not rewrite past appointments. A line paid with a package costs nothing.

fields.label: Requires vaccines up to date
fields.reason: The requirement in force when the service was booked; changing the catalog must not suddenly block or free an appointment already made.

keys.name: service
keys.message: This appointment already has this service.

entities.name: Package
entities.description: A number of credits of one service bought in advance for a pet ("4 baths"). Each appointment line paid with it uses one credit.

entities.name: WeightRecord
entities.description: The pet's weight on one day. The latest one is the pet's current weight.

fields.label: Weighing
fields.expression: if(isEmpty(measuredOn) or isEmpty(weightKg), null, concat(formatDate(measuredOn, "DD/MM/YYYY"), " · ", weightKg, " kg"))

transitions.name: appointment-approve
transitions.description: Accept an appointment the owner requested in the portal, so it is scheduled.

transitions.name: appointment-confirm
transitions.description: The owner, or the staff on the owner's behalf, confirms that the pet will come to a scheduled appointment.

transitions.name: appointment-check-in
transitions.description: The pet arrived and the service starts. Refused while a booked service requires vaccines and the pet has an overdue one.

transitions.name: appointment-ready
transitions.description: The service is finished and the pet is waiting for its owner, who is told by e-mail.

transitions.name: appointment-finish
transitions.description: The owner picked the pet up; the receipt is generated and shared with the owner in the portal.

transitions.name: appointment-cancel-requested
transitions.description: Cancel an appointment that was requested and will not happen, with the reason.

transitions.name: appointment-cancel-scheduled
transitions.description: Cancel a scheduled appointment that will not happen, with the reason.

guard.expression: coalesce(creditsUsed, 0) < credits and (isEmpty(expiresOn) or dateDiff(expiresOn, today(), "days") >= 0)
